where: crates/blaze-query/src/db/function.rs: participate, hand_over, head_round (fixpoint cycles with a head inside another head's cycle)
what: A fixpoint over nested cycles was made final one round early, so a row kept a value read from an inner head that then moved. The property test db::tests::random_cyclic_fixpoints_agree_with_a_run_from_scratch found it on a new draw (five max-nodes: 0=max(q3), 1=max(q3,q4), 2=max(in0), 3=max(in0,q0,q1), 4=max(q1); node 4 answered 0, a run from scratch gives 1). It fails on main c333c107ac and on the head b706afeffb, and still with the summary clause of Storage::holds forced false (the coordinator's run), so it is no verify shortcut: by the code read, the wrong value is computed in the new view, and a storage made with the input already at 1 answers the same (the directed test's from-scratch half says so when it is run).
cost: a lane; the answer was called a stale row and two verify-proof classes (the input summary, a cycle member's edge to its head) were suspected before the convergence test was read
cause: A row read on the stack that ends a round with another value set `unconverged` on the frame of its own lowest head (`frames[done.head]`). When that head was itself an inner head and ended a member of a lower cycle with its own value unmoved, `participate` never read the flag: it died with the frame, and the outermost head's `head_round` saw `equal(last, new) && !unconverged` hold.
whys: why wrong: row 4 read row 1's value of the round before on the stack (0); row 1 then ended the round with 1; the cycle was made final with 4 = 0
why possible: `head_round` decides on one flag on the outermost head's frame, and a moved row wrote it on its own head's frame, which is the outermost only when the cycle is not nested

why not handed on: `hand_over` is the place a member's frame gives its head what it carries (durability, untracked, summary), and the flag was written past it, straight into another frame, from `participate`

why not caught: the directed cycle tests have at most one inner head whose own value moves in the same round as its member's; the random test needs three nested heads and the right ask order, and found it only on today's draw
property: a fact a row owes the head that decides was addressed to the nearest head, by a write into another frame beside the one hand-over
class: A fact owed to the outermost head of a cycle delivered to the nearest head only: any per-round or per-cycle word written into `frames[done.head]` outside `hand_over` is lost when that head ends a member itself. Second of the class, found by reading the same line and fixed with it: `Cycle::iteration` given to `cycle_recover` was `frames[done.head].round`, which for a member of an inner head is that head's own frame's round (a new frame each outer round, so 1 in every round), not the outermost head's; no `cycle_fn` in crates/ reads it today (variances_of_cycle_fn ignores it).
prevention: A row says it moved on its OWN frame and `hand_over` hands `unconverged` to the head with the rest, each head in turn, so one function is the only writer of a head's frame from a member (function.rs participate, hand_over; local.rs Frame::unconverged says the rule). Invariant stated on the directed test db::tests::inner_heads::a_cycle_ends_only_after_a_round_in_which_no_row_read_on_the_stack_moved (every ask order, from scratch and after a write) with the control the_oracle_catches_an_inner_head_that_keeps_a_moved_row_to_itself (probe::INNER_HEADS_FORGET plants the old behaviour). The round: the run of a head kept from a cycle's last round starts its frame at the round of the head that kept it (function.rs run), and a row is told the later of its own frame's round and its head's (participate); stated on a_kept_head_is_told_the_round_of_its_cycles_outermost_head with the control the_oracle_catches_a_kept_head_that_counts_its_rounds_from_one_again (probe::KEPT_HEADS_START_AGAIN). Not built: a check that nothing but `hand_over` writes another frame's cycle state (a lint or a private setter on Frame).
state: the unconverged fix and its two tests: run green by the coordinator on the integration tree (cargo test -p blaze-query --lib, 264 of 265, the one failure fails on main too), and the property test's reproduce blob no longer reproduces; the iteration fix and its two tests: written, not compiled or run
